title: Proper normal pair preparation over a radicial constant extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a nonempty separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $Z\subseteq X$ a nowhere dense closed subset. There are a proper finite-type $k$-scheme $\overline X$, a dense open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], a nowhere dense closed subset $C\subseteq\overline X$ with $C\cap X=Z$, a finite purely inseparable field extension $e/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], and a proper finite-type $e$-scheme $B$ with a projective surjective $k$-morphism $r:B\to\overline X$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The scheme $B$ is a finite disjoint union of nonempty integral normal schemes and is geometrically reduced over $e$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; geometrically reduced means that every extension of the base field gives a reduced scheme. The morphism $r$ gives a bijection between the generic points of the components of $B$ and those of $\overline X$, and each corresponding residue-field extension is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. The subset $r^{-1}C$ is the support of an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], whose ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. The extension $e/k$ is trivial in characteristic zero. Purely inseparable means that in characteristic $p>0$ every element has a $p$-power lying in the smaller field, and means equality in characteristic zero. Projective uses the projective-bundle convention. Empty $Z$ is allowed. Field-extension terminology and degrees are as in [def-pc-field-tower].

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150 (compactification, reduced components, radicial constants, blowup, finite normalization), applied to the finitely many components with one common finite radicial constant extension. The compactification is chosen with C the closure of Z; including the complement of X is optional, not required.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; the base is affine and hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By the dense-compactification definition [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data] this gives $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ with $\overline X$ proper over $k$ and $X$ dense in $\overline X$. Proper includes finite type. Set $C=\overline{j(Z)}$ as a closed subset. Since $Z$ is closed in the open $X$, $C\cap X=Z$. Both $X$ and $\overline X$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], because $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (its only local ring is a field). Thus $\overline X$ has finitely many components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Each component has a generic point in $X$: its complement in the other finitely many components is a nonempty open subset of that component, which the dense open $X$ meets. No such generic point lies in $Z$, since $Z$ is nowhere dense in $X$. The equality $C\cap X=Z$ now shows that $C$ contains no component; hence it is nowhere dense.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 1, printed p.150, compactification and closure of Z; Noetherian finiteness: Stacks 01T6 and 0BA8.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-inseparable-geometric-reduction] to $\overline X/k$ and its finitely many irreducible components. Choose its single finite purely inseparable extension $e/k$, and put $T=(\overline X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}e)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Then $T$ is geometrically reduced over $e$. The reduced induced structure is the closed subscheme supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], applied to the whole base change. Properness is stable under base change and closed subschemes, so $T$ is proper over $e$, and hence finite type and Noetherian. In characteristic zero, purely inseparable means equality, so this choice has $e=k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: X 2.3 Step 1, finite radicial constants; Stacks 04KT (lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-reduced).

proof.text: Write $t:T\to\overline X$. The field map $\operatorname{Spec}e\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite: a finite $k$-basis of $e$ is a finite module generating set. Its base change is finite, and the reduction closed immersion is finite; thus $t$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite, lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], and since reduction changes no points, $t$ is a homeomorphism. The field map is universally injective by [lem-pc-spec-pure-insep-integral-radicial-surjective]; this property survives base change by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], and restriction to the reduction remains universally injective. The radicial equivalence [def-weil-radicial-morphism] therefore makes every residue extension of $t$ purely inseparable; it is finite because $t$ is finite (the residue field is a quotient of the finite-dimensional fibre algebra). In particular generic points correspond bijectively, with finite purely inseparable residue fields.

Let $T_1,\ldots,T_s$ be the reduced induced closed subschemes on the components of $T$, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The finite number $s$ is positive by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], since $X$ is nonempty and $t$ is a homeomorphism. Each $T_i$ is integral (reduced and irreducible), nonempty and proper over $e$; the last assertion is [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Set $C_i=t^{-1}C\cap T_i$ as a closed subset, and give it its reduced induced structure. It misses the generic point of $T_i$, so is nowhere dense. Its ideal $\mathcal I_i$ is quasi-coherent by the reduced-induced-structure theorem, and of finite type: on each Noetherian affine chart it is an ideal in a Noetherian ring and thus finitely generated. The complement $U_i=T_i\setminus C_i$ is a nonempty quasi-compact dense open.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 1, reduced components and the nowhere dense marking; Stacks 01J3 and 0BA8.

proof.text: Form the ordinary blowup $b_i:S_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}T_i\to T_i$. It is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] and is an isomorphism over $U_i$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]. The extended ideal $\mathcal I_i\mathcal O_{S_i}$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]; its support is $b_i^{-1}C_i$. The open $U_i$ is dense in $S_i$ by [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup], applied to this $U_i$-admissible blowup. The next step checks reducedness and integrality directly from the charts.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 1, blow up the marking; Stacks 01OF (blowing up), 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor).

proof.text: On a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T_i$, the ring $A$ is a domain. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], the nonempty blowup charts are spectra of the subalgebras $A[\mathcal I_i/a]\subseteq A_a$ for nonzero $a\in\mathcal I_i(\operatorname{Spec}A)$. These are domains; the charts with $a=0$ are empty. Thus $S_i$ is reduced. Its dense open $U_i$ is irreducible, so its closure $S_i$ is irreducible. Hence $S_i$ is nonempty integral and $b_i$ is birational. Properness over $e$ follows by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] from the properness of $b_i$ and $T_i/e$.

source.place: Tag 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme), expanded by the affine chart domains and the already established density; proper composition Tag 01W3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-chow-relatively-ample] over the field $e$ to $S_i$, which is integral, separated and finite type because it is proper over $e$. Obtain an integral $Y_i$, a proper surjection $c_i:Y_i\to S_i$, an immersion $Y_i\to\mathbf P^{n_i}_e$ and a nonempty open $V_i\subseteq S_i$ over which $c_i$ is an isomorphism. Hence $c_i$ induces equality of function fields. The scheme $Y_i$ is proper over $e$ by proper composition. Its immersion into projective space is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated], since projective space is separated, and then is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. Consequently $Y_i$ is projective over $e$. This auxiliary birational Chow modification is inserted to give an absolute projective embedding before normalizing.

source.place: Tags 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian) and 0201 (remark-chow-Noetherian (2),(3)), integral Chow model inserted into ILO X 2.3 Step 1; proper immersion closed: 01IQ.

proof.text: Let $n_i:N_i=Y_i^\nu\to Y_i$ be the normalization in its own function field, as in [def-sc-normalization]. By [lem-sc-normalization-exists] it is finite, surjective and birational. It is integral and normal: on a nonempty affine chart of $Y_i$ its normalization ring is the integral closure of a domain $A$ in $\operatorname{Frac}A$ [def-sc-normalization]; [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] with the identity field extension makes that ring an integrally closed domain, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] makes all of its local rings integrally closed domains. The closed immersion $Y_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_i}_e$ of Step 7 together with quasi-compactness of $Y_i$ (it is of finite type over $e$) says that $Y_i\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ is projective in the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism] (H-projective and quasi-compact), which is the hypothesis of [lem-fin-finite-over-projective]. By [lem-fin-finite-over-projective], with the affine Noetherian base $\operatorname{Spec}e$, the finite map $n_i$ above the projective $Y_i/e$ makes $N_i$ projective over $e$ in that convention: there is a closed immersion $N_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{m_i}_e$ over $e$. Thus $N_i$ is nonempty, integral, normal, proper and finite type over $e$, and $N_i\to T_i$ induces equality of function fields.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 1, finite normalization; Stacks 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), 034L (normal integral closure), and 01W8/087S for finite over projective above a field.

proof.text: The Cartier marking survives both $c_i$ and $n_i$ without a flatness assumption. Write $f$ for a local non-zero-divisor generator of $\mathcal I_i\mathcal O_{S_i}$. It is nonzero in $k(S_i)$. Both $Y_i$ and $N_i$ are integral and their maps to $S_i$ induce inclusions (in fact equalities) of function fields. Their affine section rings inject into these function fields by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Therefore the image of $f$ is nonzero in each target local domain and is a non-zero-divisor. The image ideal is generated by that image of $f$, so it is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Its vanishing set is exactly the inverse image of the vanishing set of $f$. Thus there is an effective Cartier divisor on $N_i$ with support $(t b_i c_i n_i)^{-1}C$.

source.place: Tag 02OO (lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined (2)), integral dominant case, with the non-zero-divisor argument written explicitly; ILO X 2.3 Step 1.

proof.text: The schemes $N_i$ remain geometrically reduced over $e$. Let $\eta_i$ be the generic point of $T_i$. There is an affine open neighbourhood $W$ of $\eta_i$ in $T$ meeting no other component. Then $W$ is an open subscheme of $T_i$ and is geometrically reduced, since after every field extension it is open in the reduced base change of $T$. Write $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its function field is $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}A$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. For every extension $L/e$, $F_i\otimes_e L$ is a localization of the reduced ring $A\otimes_e L$ and is reduced: if a fraction has nilpotent numerator, multiplying by one denominator kills a power, and reducedness kills the fraction itself. The generic stalk of $N_i$ is this same $F_i$, because $b_i,c_i,n_i$ are birational. Now [lem-pur-geometric-reducedness-from-generic-stalks] applies to the reduced integral scheme $N_i$ and proves geometric reducedness. This verifies the extra condition through every inserted birational model.

source.place: Tag 04KS (lemma-generic-points-geometrically-reduced (3)); generic fields unchanged through ILO X 2.3 Step 1.

proof.text: Set $B=\coprod_{i=1}^sN_i$ and define $r:B\to\overline X$ by the maps $t b_i c_i n_i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each summand is open and closed, so $B$ is a finite disjoint union of nonempty integral normal schemes and is geometrically reduced (after any field extension each of its open summands is reduced). The effective Cartier ideals from Step 9 define an ideal on this disjoint union by restriction to the summands; it is locally generated by their non-zero-divisor generators and has support $r^{-1}C$. Every $N_i\to T_i$ is surjective: $n_i$ and $c_i$ are surjective, and $b_i$ is proper with image containing the dense open $U_i$, hence has closed image all of $T_i$. Since the $T_i$ cover $T$ and $t$ is surjective, $r$ is surjective. Exactly one generic point is supplied by each $N_i$, and Step 3 and birationality show that they correspond bijectively to the generic points of $\overline X$ with the same finite purely inseparable residue extensions as for $t$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 1, assemble the finitely many integral models over the same field e; generic points and Cartier ideals are checked on the disjoint open summands.

proof.text: The finite disjoint union $B$ is projective over $e$. Indeed, choose the embeddings $N_i\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{m_i}_e$ from Step 8, and give one projective space $\mathbf P^M_e$, $M+1=\sum_i(m_i+1)$, disjoint blocks of homogeneous coordinates of these sizes. The linear subspace defined by setting every coordinate outside block $i$ to zero is $\mathbf P^{m_i}_e$. Distinct such subspaces are disjoint, since their simultaneous equations kill every homogeneous coordinate. Their finite union is a closed subscheme, and is the disjoint union of those subspaces: locally the other blocks are absent, so its structure sheaf restricts to that of the single block. The embeddings $N_i$ therefore give a closed immersion $B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^M_e$. Hence $B/e$ is proper and finite type by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper, def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01W8 (definition-projective, H-projective clause), explicit disjoint coordinate-block embedding over e.

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}e\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite, so is projective in the projective-bundle sense by [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle]. The structure sheaf of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is ample by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: the section $1$ has nonvanishing locus the entire affine scheme. Consequently [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes this finite field morphism H-projective. Since $B/e$ is H-projective by Step 12, [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] gives a closed immersion $\iota:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^d_k$.

Because $\overline X$ is separated over $k$, its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The graph $\Gamma_r:B\to B\times_k\overline X$ is its base change along $(r,\mathrm{id}_{\overline X})$, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The morphism $\iota\times\mathrm{id}_{\overline X}$ is another base change of a closed immersion. Their composite is a closed immersion (on affine charts the corresponding surjections of rings compose) $B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^d_k\times_k\overline X=\mathbf P^d_{\overline X}$ over $r$; the equality is fibre-product associativity in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Thus $r$ is H-projective. The finite projective space is the projective bundle of the finite free module $\mathcal O_{\overline X}^{d+1}$ [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], so $r$ is projective in the required projective-bundle convention [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Together with Steps 1--13 this proves every clause, including the empty-marking case: then each $\mathcal I_i=\mathcal O_{T_i}$, its blowup is the identity, and the Cartier ideals have empty support.

source.place: Tag 01W8 (definition-projective); graph is the base change of the separated diagonal, using the fibre-product identification of Schemes Tag 01KR. Final projectivity verification for ILO X 2.3 Step 1.
